title: Transfer: Daily Temperatures
oneLiner: For each day, how many days until a warmer one? The next greater element again, but the answer is a distance, so the stack has to remember positions.
keyTakeaway: Keep a stack of indices of days still waiting for a warmer day; their temperatures never increase from bottom to top. When day i is warmer than the day on top, that day's wait is over: pop it at index j and record i - j. Each day is pushed and popped at most once, so O(n).
explanation:
This follows Find the Next Greater Element with the answer changed. temperatures[i] is the temperature on day i. For each day, return how many days you would have to wait for a strictly warmer one, or 0 if no later day is warmer. For [73, 74, 75, 71, 69, 72, 76, 73] the answer is [1, 1, 4, 2, 1, 1, 0, 0]: after the 75 on day 2 the next warmer day is the 76 on day 6, four days later.

"First later day that is warmer" is exactly "next greater element", so the same one pass works. Walk the days left to right with a stack of days that have not found a warmer day yet. Before pushing day i, pop every day on top whose temperature is lower than temperatures[i]: day i is the first warmer day for each of them. Then push day i. Days still on the stack at the end never warm up and keep the answer 0.

The one real change is what you record. The parent stored the greater value; here you need the distance, answer[j] = i - j, so the stack must hold indices, not temperatures (you can always read the temperature back as temperatures[j]). Equal temperatures are not warmer, so pop only on a strict <, and a run of equal days waits together.

Every index is pushed once and popped at most once: O(n) time, O(n) space for the stack and the answer. Checking every later day for every day is O(n²), which is what the stack avoids.

The visualization runs [73, 74, 75, 71, 69, 72, 76, 73]; the stack shows day indices with their temperatures.

Explain why the same idea works: before you move on, write two or three sentences comparing this with Find the Next Greater Element. Why is the day that pops j always the first warmer day after j, why does the stack have to store indices now, and why is the whole pass still O(n)?

visualizationSteps.message: Push day 0 (73). It waits for a warmer day; the stack's temperatures never rise from bottom to top.
Day 1 (74) is warmer than day 0 (73) on top. Pop day 0: it waited 1 - 0 = 1 day.
Push day 1 (74). It waits for a warmer day; the stack's temperatures never rise from bottom to top.
Day 2 (75) is warmer than day 1 (74) on top. Pop day 1: it waited 2 - 1 = 1 day.
Push day 2 (75). It waits for a warmer day; the stack's temperatures never rise from bottom to top.
Push day 3 (71). It waits for a warmer day; the stack's temperatures never rise from bottom to top.
Push day 4 (69). It waits for a warmer day; the stack's temperatures never rise from bottom to top.
Day 5 (72) is warmer than day 4 (69) on top. Pop day 4: it waited 5 - 4 = 1 day.
Day 5 (72) is warmer than day 3 (71) on top. Pop day 3: it waited 5 - 3 = 2 days.
Push day 5 (72). It waits for a warmer day; the stack's temperatures never rise from bottom to top.
Day 6 (76) is warmer than day 5 (72) on top. Pop day 5: it waited 6 - 5 = 1 day.
Day 6 (76) is warmer than day 2 (75) on top. Pop day 2: it waited 6 - 2 = 4 days.
Push day 6 (76). It waits for a warmer day; the stack's temperatures never rise from bottom to top.
Push day 7 (73). It waits for a warmer day; the stack's temperatures never rise from bottom to top.
Done: [1, 1, 4, 2, 1, 1, 0, 0]. The days still on the stack never got a warmer day, so they keep 0.

recognitionSignals: "How many days (steps, positions) until something larger or smaller", asked for every position.
Next greater or next smaller element, but the answer is a distance or an index rather than the value.
gotchas: Push indices, not temperatures: the answer i - j needs the position of the waiting day.
Pop only on strictly warmer; an equal temperature does not end the wait.
Days left on the stack at the end keep 0, so fill the answer with 0 up front.
confusableWith: Monotonic Stack: Find the Next Greater Element records the warmer value itself; this records how far away it is, which is why the stack must hold indices.
Monotonic Deque: Sliding Window Maximum also keeps a decreasing run of indices, but it drops them from the front as the window moves on. Here an index leaves only when its answer is found.

complexity.note: Each day's index is pushed once and popped at most once, so the inner while loop does at most n pops in total. The stack and the answer can each hold n entries.
